anlamlar.en: to look or behave like an older relative
ornekler: She takes after her mother.
He really takes after his grandfather.

anlamlar.en: to separate something into its different parts
ornekler: He took the radio apart to fix it.
The children love taking things apart.

anlamlar.en: to remove something or someone from a place
ornekler: The waiter took away our plates.
The police took him away.

anlamlar.en: to subtract one number from another
ornekler: If you take away 3 from 10, you get 7.
Take away the cost of food and you have very little left.

anlamlar.en: to return something to the place you got it from
ornekler: I took the shirt back because it was too small.
Take these books back to the library.

anlamlar.en: to admit that something you said was wrong
ornekler: I take back what I said.
Take that back!

anlamlar.en: to make you remember a time in the past
ornekler: This song takes me back to my school days.
The smell of bread takes me back to my childhood.

anlamlar.en: to write down information
ornekler: The police officer took down my details.
Did you take down his number?

anlamlar.en: to remove something from a high place or take it apart
ornekler: We took down the Christmas decorations.
They took down the tent.

anlamlar.en: to understand and remember something
ornekler: It was too much information to take in.
I couldn't take in what he was saying.

anlamlar.en: to deceive someone
ornekler: Don't be taken in by his charm.
Many people were taken in by the advertisement.

anlamlar.en: to let someone stay in your home
ornekler: They took in two refugees.
She takes in stray cats.

anlamlar.en: to accept a particular job or responsibility
ornekler: She took on too much work.
I can't take on any more projects.

anlamlar.en: to start to employ someone
ornekler: The company is taking on new staff.
We took on three new teachers.

anlamlar.en: to begin to have a particular quality or appearance
ornekler: His face took on a worried look.
The word has taken on a new meaning.

anlamlar.en: to compete or fight against someone
ornekler: Our team will take on the champions next week.
She took on the big companies and won.

anlamlar.en: to remove something from a place
ornekler: She took out her phone.
The dentist took out two of my teeth.

anlamlar.en: to take someone to a restaurant, cinema or similar place
ornekler: He took her out for dinner.
I'm taking the kids out to the park.

anlamlar.en: to get money from a bank or to get a loan or insurance
ornekler: I took out some money from the ATM.
They took out a loan to buy a car.

anlamlar.en: to take control of a company, country or activity
ornekler: A big company has taken over the firm.
The army took over the country.

anlamlar.en: to start doing something that someone else was doing
ornekler: Can you take over the driving for a while?
She took over as manager last year.

anlamlar.en: to be involved in an activity with other people
ornekler: Thirty students took part in the competition.
Everyone took part in the discussion.

anlamlar.en: to happen, especially as planned
ornekler: The meeting will take place on Monday.
The story takes place in Paris.

anlamlar.en: to start doing a particular job or activity
ornekler: He took up golf when he retired.
She's taken up the piano.

anlamlar.en: to fill an amount of space or time
ornekler: This table takes up too much space.
The work took up most of my weekend.

anlamlar.en: to accept an offer or opportunity
ornekler: I'd like to take up your offer.
She took up the invitation to speak.

anlamlar.en: to persuade someone to do something
ornekler: She talked me into buying a new car.
Don't let him talk you into it.

anlamlar.en: to persuade someone not to do something
ornekler: My friends talked me out of leaving my job.
Can you talk him out of it?

anlamlar.en: to discuss something before making a decision
ornekler: Let's talk it over before we decide.
I need to talk things over with my wife.

anlamlar.en: to destroy a building or wall
ornekler: They tore down the old houses to build a park.
The wall was torn down in 1989.

anlamlar.en: to tear paper into small pieces
ornekler: She tore up the letter.
He tore up the contract and threw it away.

anlamlar.en: to see the difference between two very similar people or things
ornekler: I can't tell the twins apart.
It's hard to tell the two songs apart.

anlamlar.en: to speak angrily to someone because they have done something wrong
ornekler: The teacher told him off for being late.
My mom told me off for breaking the vase.

anlamlar.en: to have an idea, or to remember something
ornekler: I can't think of his name.
Can you think of a better plan?

anlamlar.en: to have an opinion about someone or something
ornekler: What do you think of my new dress?
I don't think much of his work.

anlamlar.en: to consider something carefully before deciding
ornekler: I'll think it over and let you know.
Think over the offer before you say no.

anlamlar.en: to consider all the possible results of something
ornekler: You need to think the plan through.
The idea wasn't properly thought through.

anlamlar.en: to invent or imagine something, especially an excuse
ornekler: She thought up a clever excuse.
We need to think up a name for the café.

anlamlar.en: to get rid of something you do not want
ornekler: Don't throw away those old photos.
I threw away the empty bottles.

anlamlar.en: to waste a skill or opportunity
ornekler: He threw away his chance of winning.
Don't throw away your future.

anlamlar.en: to get rid of something you do not want
ornekler: We threw out the old sofa.
I threw out all my old notes.

anlamlar.en: to force someone to leave a place
ornekler: He was thrown out of the club.
They threw him out of the restaurant.

anlamlar.en: to vomit
ornekler: He threw up after eating the fish.
I feel like I'm going to throw up.

anlamlar.en: to tie something with string or rope
ornekler: They tied up the boat.
She tied up her hair.

anlamlar.en: to keep someone busy
ornekler: I'm tied up in meetings all day.
I'm afraid she's tied up at the moment.

anlamlar.en: to put on a piece of clothing to see if it fits
ornekler: Can I try on these jeans?
She tried on five dresses.

anlamlar.en: to use something to find out if it works or if you like it
ornekler: I'd like to try out the new software.
We tried out a new restaurant.

anlamlar.en: to move your body so that you are facing the opposite direction
ornekler: She turned around and smiled at me.
Turn around and look at me.

anlamlar.en: to make a business or situation successful after it was failing
ornekler: The new manager turned the company around.
Can the team turn things around?

anlamlar.en: to not allow someone to enter a place
ornekler: Hundreds of fans were turned away at the gate.
The hotel was full, so they turned us away.

anlamlar.en: to move your face so that you are not looking at something
ornekler: She turned away in disgust.
He turned away from the window.

anlamlar.en: to return the way you came
ornekler: It got dark, so we turned back.
There's no turning back now.

anlamlar.en: to refuse an offer or request
ornekler: She turned down the job offer.
They turned down my application.

anlamlar.en: to reduce the level of sound or heat
ornekler: Can you turn down the music?
Turn the heating down a bit.

anlamlar.en: to give something to someone in authority
ornekler: Please turn in your essays by Friday.
He turned in the wallet he found to the police.

anlamlar.en: to go to bed
ornekler: I think I'll turn in now.
We turned in early.

anlamlar.en: to change and become something different
ornekler: The caterpillar turned into a butterfly.
They turned the old factory into apartments.

anlamlar.en: to stop a machine, light or supply of water by pressing a switch or turning a handle
ornekler: Turn off the lights when you leave.
Did you turn off the oven?

anlamlar.en: to leave a road and go onto another one
ornekler: Turn off at the next exit.
We turned off the main road.

anlamlar.en: to start a machine, light or supply of water
ornekler: Can you turn on the TV?
Turn on the tap and let the water run.

anlamlar.en: to suddenly attack someone
ornekler: The dog turned on its owner.
His friends turned on him.

anlamlar.en: to happen in a particular way, or to be discovered to be something
ornekler: It turned out that she was right.
The party turned out to be fun.

anlamlar.en: to come to an event
ornekler: Thousands of people turned out to see the parade.
Only ten people turned out for the meeting.

anlamlar.en: to switch off a light
ornekler: Turn out the lights before you go to bed.
She turned out the lamp.

anlamlar.en: to produce something
ornekler: The factory turns out 500 cars a day.
The school has turned out some great scientists.

anlamlar.en: to move something so that the other side is facing up
ornekler: Turn over the page.
She turned over the pancake.

anlamlar.en: to give something or someone to a person in authority
ornekler: He turned the evidence over to the police.
The thief was turned over to the authorities.

anlamlar.en: to arrive or appear somewhere, often unexpectedly
ornekler: He turned up late for the meeting.
She turned up at my house without warning.

anlamlar.en: to increase the level of sound or heat
ornekler: Turn up the radio, I love this song!
Can you turn the heating up?

anlamlar.en: to be found, especially by chance
ornekler: Don't worry, your keys will turn up.
The missing ring turned up in the garden.

anlamlar.en: to use all of something
ornekler: We've used up all the milk.
He used up all his savings.

anlamlar.en: to serve someone, especially at a table in a restaurant
ornekler: She waited on tables to pay for college.
He expects his wife to wait on him.

anlamlar.en: to leave a meeting or place suddenly, especially to show that you are angry
ornekler: He walked out of the meeting.
The workers walked out over pay.

anlamlar.en: to suddenly leave your husband, wife or partner
ornekler: Her husband walked out on her.
He walked out on his family.

anlamlar.en: to become warmer, or to make something warmer
ornekler: Let me warm up some soup.
The room will soon warm up.

anlamlar.en: to prepare for physical activity by doing gentle exercises
ornekler: Always warm up before you run.
The players are warming up.

anlamlar.en: to wash plates, dishes and other things used for eating and cooking
ornekler: I'll wash up after dinner.
Whose turn is it to wash up?

anlamlar.en: to wash your hands and face
ornekler: Go and wash up before dinner.
I need to wash up after work.

anlamlar.en: used to tell someone to be careful
ornekler: Watch out! There's a car coming.
Watch out for snakes on the path.

anlamlar.en: to gradually disappear or stop having an effect
ornekler: The pain will wear off soon.
The excitement wore off after a few days.

anlamlar.en: to use something so much that it is damaged and cannot be used any more
ornekler: My shoes have worn out.
He wore out two cars in five years.

anlamlar.en: to make someone very tired
ornekler: The children have worn me out.
You'll wear yourself out if you work so hard.

anlamlar.en: to relax after a period of work or excitement
ornekler: I read a book to wind down before bed.
It takes me a while to wind down after work.

anlamlar.en: to gradually reduce the work of a business until it closes
ornekler: The company is winding down its operations.
The project will wind down next year.

anlamlar.en: to destroy or remove something completely
ornekler: The disease wiped out the whole population.
The flood wiped out the village.

anlamlar.en: to spend time making or improving something
ornekler: She's working on a new novel.
You need to work on your pronunciation.

anlamlar.en: to do physical exercise to make your body strong
ornekler: I work out at the gym three times a week.
She works out every morning.

anlamlar.en: to understand something or find the answer by thinking
ornekler: I can't work out how to use this.
Can you work out the answer?

anlamlar.en: to develop in a particular way, especially a good way
ornekler: Don't worry, everything will work out.
Their marriage didn't work out.

anlamlar.en: to calculate an amount
ornekler: Work out how much it will cost.
I worked out that we need 20 chairs.

anlamlar.en: to cover something in paper, especially as a present
ornekler: She wrapped up the present.
Wrap up the sandwiches in foil.

anlamlar.en: to put on warm clothes
ornekler: Wrap up warm, it's freezing outside.
The children were wrapped up in scarves.

anlamlar.en: to finish an activity, meeting or agreement
ornekler: Let's wrap up the meeting.
They wrapped up the deal in a few hours.

anlamlar.en: to write something on a piece of paper so that you do not forget it
ornekler: Write down your password and keep it safe.
I wrote down her phone number.

anlamlar.en: to make the image of something appear larger, with a camera or on a screen
ornekler: Zoom in to see the details.
The camera zoomed in on her face.
